criteria.text: Diagnosis from the FDA Indications and Usage section (approval criterion 1); product-specific eligibility and medical-record documentation require manual review.
Patient is 18 years of age or older (approval criterion 2).
Submit dates of trial or inadequate response from two of: fiber supplements, stimulant laxatives, osmotic laxatives (approval criterion 3).

notes: Partial encoding from AK Amitiza (lubiprostone) or Linzess (linaclotide) Criteria Version 2; Approved 11/15/2013; Reviewed 09/19/2014 (format and reference update). effective_date retains 2019-06-10 from the archived stub.
Encoded: closed indication list, age ≥18, and trial/inadequate response from two of the fiber, stimulant, and osmotic laxative groups.

Product-specific FDA eligibility (notes only/manual review): CIC in adults for Amitiza and Linzess; OIC in adults with chronic non-cancer pain for Amitiza only; IBS-C in women ≥18 for Amitiza and in adults for Linzess. Product and sex are not predicate facts.

Documentation (notes only): diagnosis must be supported by the patient’s medical record (approval criterion 1). Submit dates of trial or inadequate response from two laxative groups (approval criterion 3).
Limitation of use (notes only): effectiveness of Amitiza for OIC in patients taking diphenylheptane opioids (e.g., methadone) has not been established.
Authorization (notes only): coverage may be approved for 12 months.

Quantity limits (notes only): Amitiza maximum 2 capsules/day, either strength (8mcg or 24mcg); Linzess IBS-C maximum one 290mcg capsule/day; Linzess CIC maximum one 145mcg capsule/day. Quantity enforcement requires manual review.

options.label: Chronic idiopathic constipation (CIC) — adults, Amitiza or Linzess
Opioid-induced constipation with chronic non-cancer pain — adults, Amitiza only
Irritable bowel syndrome with constipation (IBS-C) — Amitiza women ≥18; Linzess adults
